references.text: The expression 'קְרִאֵי מוֹעֵד' (called to the assembly) is also used here of the chosen leaders in Israel, showing that the rebels were recognized leaders among the people.
A review of Korah's rebellion mentions the 250 men who rose up against Moses and describes them as 'קְרִיאֵי הָעֵדָה' (those called by the congregation).
Describes the judgment on the 250 men who offered incense, confirming the number mentioned in verse 2.
The daughters of Zelophehad refer to this event and mention Korah's group that gathered against the Lord.
The psalm recalls the rebellion against Moses in the camp and the judgment that followed, with fire consuming the wicked.
Jude's letter warns against those who perished in Korah's rebellion (τῇ ἀντιλογίᾳ τοῦ Κόρε), as a warning against disobedience to God's appointed leaders.
